hook.line: Bogotá is grey half the year, so the first thing anyone asks about a flat is the light. Doña Gloria has found Tomás one, and she's selling it hard.
hook.es: El apartamento tiene mucha luz y vista a los cerros.
hook.en: The flat gets lots of light and has a view of the hills.

examples.en: The living room doesn't get much light.

examples.es: Mi cuarto tiene vista a la calle.
examples.en: My room looks out onto the street.

examples.es: La habitación es oscura, pero amplia.
examples.en: The room is dark, but spacious.
Does the flat have a view?

rule:
English says a flat gets light or is bright. Spanish says it has light: *tiene mucha luz*, *tiene poca luz*. Keep *luz* singular; *luces* are lamps.

A view works the same way: *tiene vista a* + the place. *Tiene vista a los cerros* (the hills east of Bogotá), *tiene vista al parque*.

Or describe the room with *es*: *es oscuro*, *es amplio*, *es luminoso*, *es iluminado*. These words match the room: *la cocina es oscura*, *los cuartos son amplios*.
smallPrint: In Spain you'll read *con vistas al mar*, in the plural. In Colombia people say *tiene vista a…*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *luz* or *luces* and type the whole sentence: *El apartamento tiene mucha ___.* (The flat gets lots of light.)
yourTurn.why: Daylight is *luz*, singular; *luces* would be lamps.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *oscuro* or *oscura* and type the whole sentence: *La cocina es ___.*
yourTurn.why: *Cocina* is a *la* word, so the describing word ends in *a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The flat has a view of the hills.
yourTurn.answer: El apartamento tiene vista a los cerros.
accept: El apartamento tiene una vista a los cerros.
yourTurn.why: A view is something the flat has: *tiene vista a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The living room doesn't get much light.
accept: La sala no tiene mucha luz.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask about a flat: Does it get lots of light?
yourTurn.why: Same words as the statement; the question marks do the asking.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The room is dark, but spacious.
yourTurn.answer: La habitación es oscura, pero amplia.
accept: La habitación es oscura pero amplia.
El cuarto es oscuro, pero amplio.
El cuarto es oscuro pero amplio.
yourTurn.why: Both words describe the room, so they match it: *oscura*, *amplia*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about all the rooms: *El cuarto es amplio y luminoso.*
yourTurn.answer: Los cuartos son amplios y luminosos.
yourTurn.why: Plural rooms take *son*, and both describing words add *s*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Muchas luces* is lots of lamps; daylight is *mucha luz*.
Light is something the flat has, so *tiene*.
